# Jubilees Chapter 38 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob overcomes the kings of Canaan; Esau falls by Jacob's hand

---

**38:1** In the second year of the first week of the forty-sixth jubilee, Jacob returned to Seir to make peace with Esau.

**38:2** And behold, the sons of Esau set up an ambush for Jacob. And when Jacob came near Seir, Esau's sons fell upon him with a great multitude.

**38:3** And Jacob called upon the LORD his God and the LORD hearkened to him and helped him. And a great fire went out before Jacob and burned up all the sons of Esau who had set up the ambush.

**38:4** And when Esau saw that his sons had been burned, he was greatly afraid, and he came out against Jacob.

**38:5** And Jacob said to him: "I am coming against thee in peace, not in war. Let there be peace between us."

**38:6** And Esau would not hear. And they fought, and Judah drew his bow and shot Esau in the right breast. And Esau fell and died on the mountain of Aduram.

**38:7** And Jacob buried him on the mountain of Aduram, and the sons of Esau returned to their land.

**38:8** And Canaan saw all that Jacob had done and was afraid, and they submitted to Jacob and paid tribute to Jacob.

**38:9** And Jacob ruled over the whole land of Canaan from the river to the sea, and all its peoples submitted to Jacob.

**38:10** And there was no king in Canaan who was able to raise his head against Jacob. And Jacob commanded his sons to observe the commandments and statutes of God.

**38:11** And the land was subdued before Jacob, and there was peace in the land of Canaan all the days of Jacob.

**38:12** And Jacob gathered all his sons, and Judah came before him with great joy because he had shot Esau with his bow.

**38:13** And Jacob blessed Judah and said: "Thou art my firstborn in strength and in deeds. And thy brother Esau is dead, and I have given thee all his possessions."

**38:14** "The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet, until he comes whose it is, and to whom is the obedience of the nations."

---

*EMET notes: Jubilees' account of Esau's death at Judah's hands is unique; it explains the Genesis 49:8-12 blessing of Judah as a reward for killing Esau. The fire from heaven (v.3) is a miraculous element. The Shiloh oracle (v.14) quotes Genesis 49:10 directly, placing it in the context of the Esau war.*
